Claire — thanks for the clear deck and inventory. Quick readthrough below; I'll highlight open decisions and a suggested minimum viable handoff matrix.

High level feedback (quick bullets):
- Control plane agent: yes, a lightweight agent is supported. It needs an outbound mTLS channel to Redwood control endpoints. It should be allowed to speak to our control plane on TCP 443 and TCP 7443 (agent management + metrics ingestion).
- Data plane connectivity: inference nodes require stable long‑lived connections for KV cache and websocket streaming. NAT with frequent ephemeral port churn increases reconnects; we recommend either 1:1 NAT for inference clusters or an egress gateway that preserves source IP/port affinity for the session pools.
- Ports/protocols: primarily TLS (443) with occasional gRPC (7443) and HTTP for healthchecks. If you enforce a strict egress proxy, allow websocket upgrade and larger idle timeouts (30+ minutes) for streaming jobs.
- Observability: we support Prometheus-compatible scraping via a metrics proxy, and Zipkin/OTLP tracing. For private deploys we can expose a metrics sink over mTLS to a customer collector (recommended).

Open decisions / asks from your side (please confirm):
1) Will you provide a routable SNAT mapping per inference cluster (preferred) or do you plan to place clusters behind a shared NAT?
2) Do you require us to host the control plane endpoints in your VPC (private link) or is outbound-only to Redwood-hosted endpoints acceptable under your policy?
3) Any strict egress filtering (layer 7) or TLS interception planned? That will break signature validation between our agent and runtime.

I attached a short handoff matrix (control-data-handoff-matrix.xlsx) with columns: component, expected addressability, port, session behavior, observability hook, and owner. I filled in our defaults — please edit on your side and return.

Next steps: Jonas and Kimberly will pick out any network hardening notes and we can propose a short canary plan for traffic shaping. If useful, I'll schedule a 30m call.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Adding a few operational details from the Dedicated/Private playbook that are relevant:

- Session stickiness: our runtime supports intra-request affinity via a session token in the TLS handshake at the application layer (not IP). That reduces dependency on 1:1 NAT but requires L4 pass-through for client certs.
- Idle timeouts: Recommend setting egress proxies to 60m or support TCP keepalive. Otherwise streaming SDKs will reconnect and may drop in-flight context.
- TLS interception: if you do a TLS MITM (i.e. corporate TLS proxy), we must install a Redwood-trusted cert on the proxy or use mutual TLS to the data plane to maintain integrity.
- HA considerations: plan for at least two egress gateways per region with BGP anycast or DNS failover; we can gracefully degrade to a lower-throughput model variant if connectivity degrades.

Small note on observability: please include the metrics collector IPs in the handoff matrix. We prefer a pull model over push for private deploys (customer collector scrapes).

Kimberly Park
Senior PM, Product Ops — Redwood Optimizations
